title: $\Qlb$ compact-support base change
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be separated of finite type, $g:Y'\to Y$ arbitrary
and $K\in\Dbc(X,\Qlb)$, with the finite-level hypotheses of
[thm-cbc-finite-extension] at every finite stage. The
descended exchange transformation of
[prop-weil-pbc-descent-functors] is an isomorphism

$$
Lg^*Rf_!K\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rf'_!Lg'^*K
\quad\text{in }\Dbc(Y',\Qlb).
$$

If $K$ is represented by a pair $(E,K_E)$ with
$K_E\in\Dbc(X,E)$, the map is represented
after a finite overfield $M$ by the $M$-coefficient isomorphism of
[thm-cbc-finite-extension] applied to $T_{M/E}K_E$; the result
is independent of $E$, $M$, and the representative.

proof.text:
Work at the coefficient stages and on the completed pro-etale/raw rational categories of [thm-cbc-finite-extension]. The hypotheses in the statement are exactly its hypotheses at every stage: the compact-support square and its chosen compactifications, noetherian finite-dimensional schemes with $\ell$ invertible, separated finite-type $f$, and arbitrary $g$. Write $H_{h,E}=Rh_{!,E}$ and $P_{u,E}=Lu^*_{\mathrm{comp},E}$. At each finite stage that theorem supplies the actual rational exchange
$$\eta_E:U_E=P_{g,E}H_{f,E}\Rightarrow V_E=H_{f',E}P_{g',E},$$
which is natural in every rational morphism and has invertible components. The $\Qlb$ category in this argument is exactly the raw pair category of [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category], formed from these same finite-stage categories.

source.place: Finite-stage isomorphy and the common-stage category; domain check

proof.text:
Apply [lem-cbc-rational-compact-support-coefficient-coherence] to this square. It gives the exact coherent comparisons $b^f_{M/E}$ and $b^{f'}_{M/E}$ for compact support, and the pullback comparisons $d^g_{M/E},d^{g'}_{M/E}$ used in its statement. In particular the composite comparisons $b^U,b^V$ satisfy
$$\eta_{M,T^X_{M/E}K_E}\,b^U_{M/E,K_E}=b^V_{M/E,K_E}\,T^{Y'}_{M/E}(\eta_{E,K_E}).$$
This is a comparison of the specified completed-then-rationalized exchange maps, rather than only of their endpoints. The unit, associator and shift equations in that lemma are precisely the coherence required for descent. The missing argument in the source is coefficient coherence for completed coefficient sheaves; its displayed finite-ring projection formula alone does not apply to $\mathcal O_E$ or $E$.

source.place: Opening scalar-extension paragraph, with its missing completed-coefficient coherence isolated

proof.text: Use [prop-weil-pbc-descent-functors] first for each family $H_{h,E}$ and $P_{u,E}$ with the comparisons of step 2. Its general assertion gives their descended exact functors. Composing them gives descended functors $\overline U,\overline V$, whose coefficient comparisons are $b^U,b^V$; these are the two composites in the statement. The compatibility equation in step 2 makes $(\eta_E)_E$ a compatible natural transformation, so the same proposition descends it to $\overline\eta:\overline U\Rightarrow\overline V$. At an object $(E,K_E)$ of [def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category], its component is $[E,\eta_{E,K_E}]$. Thus it is the descended exchange specified by the statement, with no identification with a different ambient sheaf or Karoubi category.

source.place: Descent of the coherent functors and of the exchange transformation

proof.text:
By [thm-cbc-finite-extension], $v_E=\eta_{E,K_E}^{-1}$ exists in $\mathcal C_E(Y')$. Composition and identity in [def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category] give
$$[E,v_E][E,\eta_{E,K_E}]=[E,v_E\eta_{E,K_E}]=[E,1],\qquad [E,\eta_{E,K_E}][E,v_E]=[E,1].$$
Consequently $\overline\eta_{(E,K_E)}$ is an isomorphism for every object. The inverse equations, rather than any exactness or idempotent-completeness assertion about the colimit, prove invertibility.

source.place: Passage of the finite-stage inverse to the common-stage category

proof.text:
For a finite $M\supset E$, step 2 rewrites as
$$T^{Y'}_{M/E}(\eta_{E,K_E})=(b^V_{M/E,K_E})^{-1}\,\eta_{M,T^X_{M/E}K_E}\,b^U_{M/E,K_E}.$$
The left side represents the same morphism as $[E,\eta_{E,K_E}]$ by [def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category], since both endpoints initially have coefficient field $E$ and $T_{E/E}=1$. The right side says exactly that under the prescribed coefficient identifications of source and target this representative is the $M$-coefficient isomorphism applied to $T_{M/E}K_E$. The associator equation of [lem-cbc-rational-compact-support-coefficient-coherence] makes these identifications consistent under $M\subset N$. For two nonnested choices, enlarge to their compositum, which is an allowed common stage by the pair-category definition. They then represent the same map, proving independence of $M$.

source.place: The finite-overfield representative and independence of its stage

proof.text:
It remains to spell out independence of the pair representing the fixed object $K$. Fix representing isomorphisms $\alpha_E:(E,K_E)\xrightarrow{\sim}K$ and $\alpha_L:(L,K_L)\xrightarrow{\sim}K$. The common-stage calculus [prop-weil-pbc-common-stage-calculus] realizes $\alpha_L^{-1}\alpha_E$ and its inverse, with their two identity equations, at one finite stage $M$. Thus it is represented there by an isomorphism $u:T^X_{M/E}K_E\xrightarrow{\sim}T^X_{M/L}K_L$. The finite-stage naturality in [thm-cbc-finite-extension] is the equation
$$V_M(u)\,\eta_{M,T_{M/E}K_E}=\eta_{M,T_{M/L}K_L}\,U_M(u).$$
Put $w=\alpha_L^{-1}\alpha_E$. By the morphism formula of [prop-weil-pbc-descent-functors], $\overline V(w)$ is represented at $M$ by $(b^V_{M/L})^{-1}V_M(u)b^V_{M/E}$, and $\overline U(w)$ is represented by $(b^U_{M/L})^{-1}U_M(u)b^U_{M/E}$. Substitute the step-5 formula for each transported exchange component into the two composites $\overline V(w)\overline\eta_{(E,K_E)}$ and $\overline\eta_{(L,K_L)}\overline U(w)$. After cancellation of adjacent comparison inverses, their $M$-representatives are respectively $(b^V_{M/L})^{-1}V_M(u)\eta_{M,T_{M/E}K_E}b^U_{M/E}$ and $(b^V_{M/L})^{-1}\eta_{M,T_{M/L}K_L}U_M(u)b^U_{M/E}$. The displayed finite-stage naturality equation identifies them. Therefore in the descended category
$$\overline V(\alpha_L^{-1}\alpha_E)\,\overline\eta_{(E,K_E)}=\overline\eta_{(L,K_L)}\,\overline U(\alpha_L^{-1}\alpha_E).$$
The conjugated maps are exactly the images of the input comparison by the explicit morphism formula of [prop-weil-pbc-descent-functors]. Multiplication by $\overline V(\alpha_L)$ on the left and $\overline U(\alpha_E)^{-1}$ on the right therefore identifies the two maps to the fixed endpoints for $K$. Changing the morphism representative or enlarging $M$ does not change these classes by the common-stage calculus and descent. This proves independence of $E$ and of the representative, relative to its specified identification with $K$, entirely inside the same raw PBC coefficient categories.

source.place: Final independence clause, with representing isomorphisms and naturality written explicitly
